No people, no text, no logos, no UI controls. This is speculative artwork, not a documentary photograph. Direction: sophisticated editorial art, a tactile ink-and-watercolour architectural collage on warm ivory paper. Render the hall's sweeping terraces as finely drawn charcoal architectural lines with restrained honey-gold washes. The central oval stage becomes a richly detailed teal ocean atlas with bathymetric contour lines and currents, extending delicately through the hall. Integrate one large hand-engraved humpback whale, one sperm whale and a small group of dolphins, swimming through the hall and across the cartographic sea; they are elegant biological illustrations, not cute mascots. Echo measured sound contours in a few subtle flowing ink lines that join the animals to the central stage. Clean negative space, excellent hierarchy, contemporary arts-publication sensibility, limited palette of ivory, ink, muted teal and brass. No labels, no typography, no musical note symbols.
